<!--
WRITTEN 2026-08-11 (Luciano). Third encoding of the same 840 marks as figure_5.Rmd, and the point of
having three is that the body figure can only put ONE of the three design axes on the rows. This one
puts the CHANNEL COUNT there. Column = member, row = N_ch, colour = the acquisition interval, and the
instrumental noise is not drawn at all.

WHAT NOISE THEN IS, since it is not gone from the data. It is what moves a mark along the horizontal
axis: within one panel and one colour, the points are the noise sweep at a fixed channel count and a
fixed sampling rate, from the highest noise at tau_int near 1 to the lowest noise at the right end.
So the figure has all 210 cells per member, exactly as figure_5.Rmd, and reads the noise axis as
position rather than as a key. THE THIN PATH JOINS THAT SWEEP, in order of noise and NOT in order of
tau_int, which is the honest order. Measured over the 28 (N_ch, interval) pairs of the grid,
tau_int falls monotonically with noise at 19 of them; at the other 9 there is a single step in the
wrong direction and it is at most 0.033 in tau_int, median 0.0095, against sweeps that span up to
16.4. So the exceptions are the estimation error of the statistic and not a reversal of the sweep,
and ordering the path by tau_int instead would hide that by construction.

WHAT THIS ENCODING IS FOR, and it is a different question from the body figure's. Reading down a
column asks whether the distortion depends on how many channels are in the patch once the memory in
the residual is held fixed. MEASURED 2026-08-11, second chunk below: it does not, and that is the
result this variant exists to carry. Interpolating log magnitude against log tau_int separately for
each channel count and comparing the four curves at a common tau_int and a fixed sampling rate, the
largest gap anywhere is a factor of 1.06 for ILSE, 1.15 for INR and 1.08 for IR, with medians over
the seven intervals of 1.02, 1.06 and 1.02. The four rows really are one picture drawn four times.
That is what licenses the body figure to pool the channel counts into one panel and to ask the reader
for two numbers rather than three: tau_int and the sampling rate, not the patch size.

R IS THE EXCEPTION AND IT IS THE CORNER AGAIN. Its gap reaches 1.81, at the coarsest sampling, where
it is carrying the ill-conditioned cell (N_ch = 10^4, Delta_tilde = 1) that figure_5.Rmd's header
records as the one edit that file still owes. Read the bottom-left of the R column as that cell and
not as a channel-count effect.

WHAT IS NOT THE SAME DOWN THE COLUMN, and it is a shape statement rather than a size one: IR's
anisotropy reaches 1.15 in 9 of the 210 cells drawn here, 6 of them at N_ch = 10 and the other 3 at
N_ch = 100, every one at the lowest noise on the grid, worst 1.31; at N_ch of 10^3 and 10^4 there are
none and the maximum falls to 1.10 and 1.07. That is the Gaussian moment closure on the occupancy
going at few channels, which 00_abstract.tex already states. It does not show in this figure's
points, only in the length of their bars, which is the same trap figure_5.Rmd's header names.
(The body's count of 28 such cells is over 294 source cells at both anchors; these 9 are the pool
anchor and the 210 cells this figure draws. Different sets, not a disagreement.)

Shares every number with figure_5.Rmd: same source files, same anchor (pool), same four members, same
shared axes. Do not re-derive anything here; if the data block has to change, change it there first.
Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
KEEP <- names(LAB)

# strip and key labels: plain from 0.01 to 100, powers outside; parsed as plotmath below.
pw10 <- function(x) {
  e <- round(log10(x))
  ifelse(abs(e) <= 2, format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), sprintf("10^%d", e))
}

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% KEEP) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))),
         n_strip = factor(sprintf("N[ch] == %s", pw10(Num_ch)),
                          levels = sprintf("N[ch] == %s", pw10(sort(unique(Num_ch))))))

cat(sprintf("figure_5_Nch: %d marks over %d cells in %d panels; per member: %s\n",
            nrow(dat), n_distinct(dat[c("noise","Num_ch","interval_in_tau")]),
            nlevels(dat$member) * nlevels(dat$n_strip),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
cat(sprintf("rows: %s ; marks per row and member: %s\n",
            paste(levels(dat$n_strip), collapse = " | "),
            paste(as.integer(table(dat$Num_ch)) / nlevels(dat$member), collapse = " ")))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 5.2}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey45") +
  # the path is the noise sweep at fixed channel count and interval, ordered by noise.
  geom_path(aes(group = d), linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.55,
            data = ~ arrange(.x, member, Num_ch, d, as.numeric(noise))) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(n_strip ~ member, labeller = labeller(n_strip = label_parsed)) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10), labels = c("1", "2", "5", "10")) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100),
                labels = c("0.3", "1", "3", "10", "30", "100")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(widetilde(Delta)), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  # sizes written out rather than left to base_size: eLife's 7 pt floor is on the drawn text.
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7))

ggsave("Figure_5_Nch.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 5.2, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
dat %>% group_by(member, Num_ch) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            size_med = median(mag), size_min = min(mag), size_max = max(mag),
            shape_med = median(aniso), frac_ge_115 = mean(mag >= 1.15), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\ncells whose anisotropy reaches 1.15, by member and channel count (the bar, not the point):\n")
dat %>% group_by(member, Num_ch) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_shape_ge_115 = sum(aniso >= 1.15), shape_max = max(aniso), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

# Does the channel count move the distortion AT A COMMON tau_int? That is the figure's question, and
# it cannot be answered by comparing cells at a common NOISE, because the same noise leaves different
# memory at different channel counts. So interpolate each row's curve and compare them where they
# overlap in tau_int, one sampling rate at a time.
gap_over_Nch <- function(g) {
  ks <- split(g, g$Num_ch)
  ks <- ks[sapply(ks, function(k) nrow(k) >= 3)]
  if (length(ks) < 2) return(tibble(gap = NA_real_, at_tau = NA_real_))
  lo <- max(sapply(ks, function(k) min(k$tau_int)))
  hi <- min(sapply(ks, function(k) max(k$tau_int)))
  if (!(hi > lo * 1.05)) return(tibble(gap = NA_real_, at_tau = NA_real_))
  xs <- 10^seq(log10(lo), log10(hi), length.out = 25)
  ys <- sapply(ks, function(k) approx(log10(k$tau_int), log10(k$mag),
                                      xout = log10(xs), ties = mean)$y)
  r <- 10^(apply(ys, 1, max) - apply(ys, 1, min))
  tibble(gap = max(r), at_tau = xs[which.max(r)])
}

cat("\nlargest disagreement between the four channel counts at a COMMON tau_int, per sampling rate:\n")
gaps <- dat %>% group_by(member, d) %>% group_modify(~ gap_over_Nch(.x)) %>% ungroup()
gaps %>% as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
cat("\nsummary of that gap per member (1 would be an exact collapse of the four rows):\n")
gaps %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(med_gap = median(gap, na.rm = TRUE), max_gap = max(gap, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```

```{r collapse}
# THE COLLAPSE, EXTENDED TO THE FULL LADDER. The owner of this measurement is figure_5.Rmd's collapse
# chunk, which is what 04_results cites and what Figure 5 supplement 2 draws. This copy exists for one
# reason: the body sentence says "every member" and figure_5.Rmd only reads the four it draws, so the
# other four are checked here. If the two ever disagree, figure_5.Rmd is right and this is stale.
# (On 2026-08-11 the citation pointed at a chunk that did not exist in any file; it does now.)
#
# The test is not the same as the interpolation above and is stronger: the battery contains cells
# that share r = S_tilde/N_ch at different (noise, N_ch), for instance noise 10 at N_ch 10 and noise
# 100 at N_ch 100. Those are SEPARATE simulations of different preparations. If the ratio is the
# only thing that matters they must land on the same tau_int and the same distortion, and there is
# no fitting or interpolation in between, so agreement is the whole content.
#
# Run over the FULL ladder, not just the four members drawn, because the body's sentence says
# "every member". Anchor and files as everywhere else in this family.
LAB_ALL <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
             macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")

all8 <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", param == "mag") %>%
  transmute(member = factor(unname(LAB_ALL[algo]), levels = unname(LAB_ALL)),
            noise = as.numeric(noise), Num_ch, interval_in_tau, mag = m) %>%
  inner_join(mutate(tau, noise = as.numeric(noise)),
             by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), mag > 0) %>%
  mutate(r = noise / Num_ch)   # the label cancels in the ratio, so r is the same in either unit

shared <- all8 %>% group_by(member, interval_in_tau, r) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>% ungroup()
cat(sprintf("cells sharing an r with a different (noise, N_ch): %g of %g per member, over %d r values\n",
            nrow(shared) / nlevels(all8$member), nrow(all8) / nlevels(all8$member),
            n_distinct(shared$r)))

cat("\ntau_int at matched r (this is the axis of the figure, and it is member-independent):\n")
shared %>% filter(member == "ILSE") %>% group_by(interval_in_tau, r) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(tau_int) / min(tau_int), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(n = n(), min = min(spread), median = median(spread), max = max(spread)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 4)

cat("\ndistortion at matched r, per member, with and without the coarsest sampling:\n")
bind_rows(
  shared %>% mutate(set = "all intervals"),
  shared %>% filter(interval_in_tau < 1) %>% mutate(set = "excluding Delta_tilde = 1")
) %>%
  group_by(set, member, interval_in_tau, r) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(mag) / min(mag), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(set, member) %>%
  summarise(median = median(spread), max = max(spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = c(median, max)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nwhere the worst one is, since it decides whether the sentence needs a qualifier:\n")
shared %>% group_by(member, interval_in_tau, r) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(mag) / min(mag),
            worst_pair = paste(sprintf("N_ch=%g", range(Num_ch)), collapse = " vs "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(spread, n = 5) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
